target.title: fix(ui): queue chat input while reconnecting
target.body:
Closes #102700

## What Problem This Solves

The Control UI kept its reconnect queue alive, but disabled the composer whenever the Gateway disconnected. Users therefore could not add new text or attachments during intermittent connectivity even though the existing queue and session-scoped persistence could safely hold them.

Storage failure was also implicit. An input could appear queued even when browser quota, privacy mode, attachment serialization, or the 50-item bound prevented the exact reconnect item from being stored.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Separate compose availability from live Gateway availability.
- Allow ordinary text and attachment sends to enter the existing per-gateway/session/agent reconnect queue while disconnected.
- Keep slash commands, voice, compaction, goal edits, retry, and steer controls connection-gated.
- Read back the exact queued item before clearing offline input. If storage fails, restore the full composer payload when safe; otherwise keep the item visibly failed without overwriting newer draft work.
- Preserve one idempotency key across reconnect and consume reply context once the queued turn owns it.
- Add deterministic mocked-Gateway online/offline control and browser evidence output.

This reuses the existing bounded queue and current-tab session storage. It does not add cold offline app launch, cross-tab/background sync, or a new storage subsystem.

## User Impact

During an intermittent Gateway outage, an already-loaded Control UI remains writable. Ordinary text and attachments show as **Waiting for reconnect**, survive a same-tab refresh when storage succeeds, and send once after the socket reconnects. If browser storage cannot safely retain the input, the UI does not claim success or silently discard the only copy.

Mobile audit, unchanged by this PR:

- iOS already has a SQLite-backed submitted-message outbox with route scoping, reconnect replay, idempotency, and retry/delete UI. Unsubmitted composer text remains memory-only, and kill/relaunch UI E2E coverage is still missing.
- Android has a Room-backed offline text outbox and reconnect replay, but healthy online sends bypass that durable journal; drafts and offline attachments remain memory-only, and the destructive migration path can erase the queue. Follow-up should journal every text send before network dispatch and replace destructive migration.

## Evidence

- `corepack pnpm test ui/src/pages/chat/chat-send.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/composer-persistence.test.ts`: 117 passed after the final recovery hardening.
- Focused composer/view/send/persistence/helper suite: 264 passed on the rebased feature.
- `OPENCLAW_BEHAVIOR_PROOF=1 corepack pnpm test ui/src/e2e/chat-flow.e2e.test.ts`: 37 passed after the final commit.
- Source-blind behavior proof: composer/send enabled offline; prompt and waiting state stored; 0 offline requests; exactly 1 request after reconnect; idempotency key present; queue cleared after delivery.
- Path-scoped `check:changed`: core and test typechecks, sharded lint, docs/policy/dependency/storage/import guards passed.
- Final targeted core/test `tsgo`, `oxlint`, formatting, and `corepack pnpm build`: passed.
- Autoreview: clean after fixing storage-quota, stale slash-menu, retry-only, and concurrent-draft recovery findings.
- Testbox: `tbx_01kx38dav7vwrv14xea5hgx848`.
- Visual scenario: offline queued state and delivered-after-reconnect state captured from a real Chromium run; artifact links follow on this PR.

## AI Assistance

Codex assisted with implementation, regression tests, mobile/web source audits, source-aware review, and source-blind behavior validation. No transcript is attached.
